grade.rationale: The document is a valid, minimal Angular application shell with appropriate charset, language, base URL, viewport, favicon, and root component declarations. The only notable issue is the generic page title.

observations.summary: The HTML is correct, concise, and maintainable. Replace the placeholder-like title with a product-specific name to improve clarity, accessibility, and identification in browser tabs and bookmarks. Test coverage is unknown and was not scored as absent.

findings.title: Document title is too generic
findings.description: The title "Frontend" does not meaningfully identify the application. This reduces clarity in browser tabs, bookmarks, history entries, and assistive navigation contexts.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with the product or application name, or configure the Angular application to set a descriptive route-specific title.

grade.rationale: The entry point is concise, idiomatic Angular bootstrap code with correct dependency wiring and explicit handling of bootstrap rejection. No actionable defect is evident in the supplied content.

observations.summary: No findings. The file cleanly bootstraps the Angular application and reports startup failures. Test coverage is unknown, but the absence of coverage data does not indicate a problem in this minimal composition root.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet is syntactically coherent and uses a well-structured design-token palette, but it has accessibility and maintainability defects affecting disclosure affordances, text contrast, form-control consistency, and selector scope.

observations.summary: The CSS is generally organized and theme-aware. The main risks are inaccessible low-contrast microcopy, removal of the native details disclosure marker, incomplete form-font normalization, and an overly broad descendant selector. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied, and the unavailable ESLint run does not establish a defect in this file.

findings.title: Dim text token fails contrast for very small UI text
findings.description: The dim foreground is approximately 2.8:1 against the light surface and about 3.1:1 against the dark surface, yet it is used for 9px eyebrow text. This is below the 4.5:1 contrast expected for normal-sized text and makes labels especially difficult to read.
findings.recommendation: Use a higher-contrast dim foreground for textual content and raise microcopy to a practical minimum size. Keep the existing dim token only for non-text decoration if that lower emphasis is required, and verify both themes with automated contrast checks.

findings.title: Flex styling removes the native disclosure marker
findings.description: Changing a details element's direct summary from its default list-item display to flex removes the browser-provided disclosure triangle. Without a replacement indicator, users may not recognize that the repository risk view can be expanded or collapsed.
findings.recommendation: Preserve `display: list-item` and place the flex layout in a child wrapper, or add an explicit accessible marker whose state changes for `details[open]`. Verify keyboard focus and open/closed states visually.

findings.title: Global font normalization omits select and textarea controls
findings.description: Only buttons and inputs inherit the application font. Selects and textareas that do not later receive a complete `font` shorthand can therefore use browser-default font families or line heights, producing inconsistent controls across platforms.
findings.recommendation: Include `select` and `textarea` in the global inheritance rule, then override typography only where a component intentionally differs.

findings.title: Pane header selector styles every nested div
findings.description: `.pane-header div` applies the column flex layout to all descendant div elements, including future wrappers or control containers. Adding nested markup can therefore change layout unexpectedly without touching this stylesheet.
findings.recommendation: Target the intended direct child with `.pane-header > div`, or assign a semantic class such as `.pane-header-title` and style that class explicitly.

grade.rationale: The configuration is concise, idiomatic Angular code with correctly composed providers and no evident functional defects. Automated ESLint evidence was unavailable, and test coverage is unknown, but neither limitation establishes a code issue.

observations.summary: No actionable issues were identified. The file cleanly configures global browser error listeners, coalesced zone change detection, routing, and HTTP services.

grade.rationale: The template is generally well structured and uses Angular control flow, semantic controls, labels, stable tracking keys, and accessible names effectively. The main concerns are an invalid ARIA menu structure, unguarded dismissal of an editable dialog, and dry-run validation that is weaker than the form's declared constraints. Test coverage is unknown.

observations.summary: The UI composition is mostly correct and clear, but repository-menu semantics should be repaired, guideline edits should be protected from accidental dismissal, and dry runs should share the form's complete validation contract.

findings.title: Repository menu contains controls without menu-item roles
findings.description: The element with role="menu" contains action buttons whose implicit role remains "button" rather than an allowed menu-item role. The heading and action container are also not represented using menu-compatible semantics. This produces an inconsistent accessibility tree and can prevent assistive-technology menu navigation from recognizing all available actions.
findings.recommendation: Either implement the complete ARIA menu pattern by giving every actionable descendant an appropriate menuitem role and supporting menu keyboard behavior, or remove role="menu" and use ordinary button/list semantics for this popup.

findings.title: Backdrop dismissal can discard guideline edits without a guard
findings.description: Clicking the backdrop writes the dialog-open signal directly, bypassing any opportunity to detect dirty form state or confirm that pending guideline changes should be discarded. This makes accidental data loss possible during editing.
findings.recommendation: Route every dismissal path through one close handler. Track whether the form differs from its initial value and request confirmation before closing when it is dirty; also use the same handler for the close button and Escape-key handling.

findings.title: Dry run bypasses most declared guideline constraints
findings.description: The dry-run button is enabled whenever the ID and content are non-empty, even when the ID fails its pattern, priority is missing or out of range, or the required kinds and levels are empty. Because it is type="button", native form submission validation does not protect this action, so malformed requests can reach the handler.
findings.recommendation: Expose the form through a template reference and disable or reject dry runs unless the entire form is valid. Prefer sharing one validation routine between dry-run and save paths so their accepted input cannot drift.

grade.rationale: The file is a minimal, valid Angular route configuration. No correctness, maintainability, clarity, error-handling, or testability defects are evident from the supplied content.

observations.summary: No actionable issues found. The exported empty Routes array is type-safe and appropriate when the application currently defines no routes. Test coverage is unknown, and ESLint evidence was unavailable because dependencies were missing; neither fact establishes a defect in this file.

grade.rationale: The component is generally readable and uses Angular signals coherently, but core initialization and file-navigation promises are not handled safely, navigation can race, invalid repository limits can be saved with altered semantics, and browser storage failures can abort component behavior. Test coverage is unknown, and ESLint evidence was unavailable.

observations.summary: The main risks are asynchronous: initialization failures become unhandled rejections, overlapping file requests can publish stale results, and several background operations lack lifecycle-aware error handling. Repository validation and global keyboard handling also have correctness gaps.

findings.title: Initialization and background refresh failures are left unhandled
findings.description: The constructor discards the promise returned by initialize(), initialize() deliberately discards the dashboard promise, and timer callbacks discard loadQuotas() promises. A rejection from any awaited startup call can therefore become an unhandled rejection and leave the application partially initialized without a visible error. The dashboard request can also reject independently after initialize() has continued.
findings.recommendation: Catch initialization failures at the constructor boundary and expose a startup error/loading state. Preserve dashboard concurrency by awaiting it later or attaching an explicit rejection handler. Wrap retry and interval callbacks in a shared error-handling method, prevent overlapping refreshes, and cancel the retry timeout during destruction.

findings.title: Overlapping file loads can apply stale navigation results
findings.description: open() starts loadFile(path) without correlating its completion with the current selection. If the user opens file A and then file B while A is still loading, A's later completion can update shared file state and this continuation can change the active review kind, finding selection, and telemetry even though B remains selected. The promise also has no rejection handler.
findings.recommendation: Give each navigation a request token or use an abortable/switch-latest loading mechanism. Before applying completion logic, verify that the completed request still matches selected(). Prefer returning file data from the API rather than rereading shared mutable state, and handle load failures with a visible error state.

findings.title: Invalid token-cap input is silently converted into no cap when saved
findings.description: When parsing fails, setDefaultTokenCap() sets defaultReviewTokenCap to null while retaining only a separate error signal. saveRepository() does not check that signal, so submission can proceed and persist null, changing an invalid value into an uncapped/default configuration rather than rejecting the form.
findings.recommendation: Do not mutate the persisted cap to null on parse failure, or maintain a separate validated draft value. Disable or reject saveRepository() while repositoryTokenCapError is non-empty, and validate all repository fields again immediately before calling the API.

findings.title: Unguarded localStorage access can prevent startup or break reactive effects
findings.description: The theme field reads localStorage during instance initialization, and layout/theme persistence writes to it without protection. localStorage can throw, including when storage is disabled or access is denied. loadLayout() already anticipates this behavior, but the other access paths do not, so component construction or a reactive update can fail.
findings.recommendation: Centralize storage access behind safe get/set helpers that catch storage exceptions and degrade to in-memory defaults. Inject that abstraction so storage failure paths are straightforward to test.

findings.title: The global Ctrl+B shortcut overrides editing behavior in form controls
findings.description: The window-level key handler always prevents Ctrl+B, including when focus is in a text input, textarea, or contenteditable region. This can suppress expected bold formatting or browser/editor behavior while users edit guideline or repository content.
findings.recommendation: Ignore the shortcut when the event target is an input, textarea, select, or contenteditable element, unless that specific control explicitly opts into the workspace shortcut. Add keyboard tests covering modifier combinations and editable targets.

grade.rationale: The utilities are concise and generally readable, but several edge cases produce misleading output or uncaught exceptions. In particular, positive infinity is rendered as a byte quantity, invalid dates throw, and token formatting accepts values that its corresponding parser rejects.

observations.summary: The ordinary input paths are straightforward, but boundary validation is inconsistent. Tightening the accepted domains and defining explicit invalid-input behavior would materially improve correctness and testability.

findings.title: Invalid date input throws during formatting
findings.description: `new Date(value)` can produce an invalid Date, and `Intl.DateTimeFormat.prototype.format` then throws a RangeError. Because the function accepts an arbitrary string and provides no validation or documented throwing contract, malformed or missing timestamp data can disrupt rendering rather than yielding a safe fallback.
findings.recommendation: Parse the value, check `Number.isNaN(date.getTime())`, and return a defined fallback such as an empty string or placeholder; alternatively, expose an explicit throwing contract and handle it at every caller.

findings.title: Positive infinity is rendered as a valid byte quantity
findings.description: The non-finite guard enters this branch for `Infinity`, but `bytes || 0` remains `Infinity` and `Math.max` preserves it, producing `"Infinity B"`. This contradicts the apparent intent to sanitize invalid byte counts and can expose misleading UI output.
findings.recommendation: Handle non-finite values separately, for example by returning `"0 B"` or an explicit unavailable-value placeholder before applying the finite-number formatting logic.

findings.title: Formatter and parser disagree on valid token quantities
findings.description: `formatTokenCount` renders zero and negative finite values, while `parseTokenCount` explicitly rejects every value that is not greater than zero. This prevents consistent round trips and permits nonsensical negative token quantities to appear in operator controls.
findings.recommendation: Define one shared domain policy. If token quantities must be positive integers, return an empty string for non-positive or non-integral formatter inputs; otherwise update the parser and documentation to support the same values.

findings.title: Separator removal silently accepts malformed numeric input
findings.description: Removing every comma and underscore before validation means strings such as `"1,,__0"`, `"_100"`, or `"10_"` are accepted as valid quantities. This can conceal user typos rather than reporting invalid input.
findings.recommendation: Validate separators in their original positions before normalization, using an explicit accepted grammar such as consistently grouped thousands separators, then remove them only after validation.

grade.rationale: The implementation is concise, readable, and safely handles nullish input, but its fallback extraction treats extensionless filenames as extensions, causing incorrect classifications for filenames such as `js` or `json`.

observations.summary: A small, mostly maintainable utility with one confirmed classification edge case. No coverage conclusions were drawn because coverage data is unavailable, and the unavailable ESLint analyzer produced no applicable finding.

findings.title: Extensionless filenames can be mistaken for language extensions
findings.description: When no dot is present, the code uses the entire lowercase filename as the lookup key. Consequently, paths such as `/tmp/js`, `/tmp/json`, or `/tmp/py` are classified as JavaScript, JSON, or Python even though those files have no extension. The special handling for single-dot files already extracts names such as `gitignore`, so using the full filename for every extensionless file is unnecessary.
findings.recommendation: Use an empty or undefined lookup key when there is no extension, while retaining explicit handling for recognized dotfiles. Add tests covering ordinary extensions, recognized dotfiles, extensionless filenames that match mapping keys, empty input, and trailing separators.

grade.rationale: The API facade is strongly typed and generally readable, but repository-scoped state can become inconsistent, overlapping requests can publish stale results, and broad fallback behavior can present fabricated preview content as real repository data. Error handling also obscures several actionable failures.

observations.summary: The service provides a comprehensive typed API surface, but its shared mutable signals need stronger request identity and repository isolation. The highest-risk cases are stale file responses overwriting newer selections, repository changes leaving data from the previous repository visible, and arbitrary HTTP failures being treated as legacy or preview mode. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was available.

findings.title: An older file request can overwrite a newer selection
findings.description: loadFile does not associate its response with the requested repository or a request sequence. If two file loads overlap, or the repository changes while a load is pending, the older response can set file and connectionState after the newer selection has taken effect. Its finally block can also clear the shared loading flag while a newer request is still running.
findings.recommendation: Capture the repository ID and a monotonically increasing file-request sequence before issuing the request. Apply the response, fallback, and loading-state changes only when both still match the active request, or cancel superseded requests with RxJS switchMap.

findings.title: Every file-loading failure is replaced with unrelated demo content
findings.description: The catch block converts all failures—including missing files, authorization failures, invalid paths, and server errors—into a successful-looking FileDocument containing the same C# demo. The document retains the requested path, so consumers can mistake fabricated content and findings for the requested repository file.
findings.recommendation: Use demo content only in an explicit application-wide preview mode established by a confirmed API-unavailable condition. For ordinary file errors, clear the file, expose a structured error signal, and preserve the HTTP status so the UI can distinguish not-found, forbidden, and transient failures.

findings.title: Repository switches retain substantial state from the previous repository
findings.description: selectRepository clears the file, attack matrix, usage, tree, and project, but leaves repository-scoped signals such as scan, risk, inputs, guidelines, traces, scope rules, review runs, and handover configuration unchanged. loadRepositoryDetails then fetches four resources with an all-or-nothing Promise.all; if any request fails, none of the successful results are applied and the old repository's values can remain visible indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Reset every repository-scoped signal when selection begins, or maintain a complete snapshot keyed by repository. Load independent resources separately so one failed endpoint cannot prevent successful responses from replacing stale state, and guard every write with the selection sequence.

findings.title: Repository registration methods change the selected ID without loading its data
findings.description: loadRepositories directly updates selectedRepositoryId. createRepository requests the newly created ID, and archiving the selected repository requests a replacement, but neither path invokes selectRepository. The selected repository metadata can therefore change while tree, project, file, runs, and other signals still describe the previous repository.
findings.recommendation: Keep loadRepositories limited to refreshing registrations and return the desired ID. Route every actual selection change through selectRepository, or centralize selection and repository-state replacement in one atomic method.

findings.title: Any repository discovery error is interpreted as a legacy server
findings.description: The catch block treats authentication errors, authorization failures, malformed responses, timeouts, and transient server failures exactly like an older server that lacks the repository registry. It then changes all subsequent endpoint construction to the legacy /api routes, masking the original failure and potentially sending later operations to incorrect endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Enable legacy routing only for a narrowly identified compatibility response, such as a confirmed 404 or unsupported-version signal. Preserve other failures as connection errors and provide an explicit retry path.

findings.title: Tree failures advertise preview data without installing it
findings.description: When the tree request fails, loadTree changes connectionState to preview and logs a demo fallback but does not assign demoTree. During repository selection the tree was already replaced with an empty array when no snapshot existed, so the UI can display an 'API offline, preview data' label while no preview tree is present.
findings.recommendation: Either explicitly assign the preview tree on the intended offline path or use the offline state and an error signal when no preview data is installed. Avoid logging a fallback that did not occur.

findings.title: Review control methods report success to callers after failures
findings.description: cancelReview, pauseReview, and resumeReview catch request failures and only update reviewError. Because their Promise<void> values still resolve, callers cannot distinguish success from failure and may close dialogs, announce success, or advance workflow state incorrectly.
findings.recommendation: After setting reviewError, rethrow the original error or return an explicit discriminated result. Apply the same error contract consistently across review mutations.

grade.rationale: The route helpers are concise, readable, and mostly preserve sensible invariants. The main weakness is incomplete numeric validation when serializing a location index.

observations.summary: The implementation is straightforward and generally correct. One low-severity edge case allows non-finite numbers to be written as invalid query-parameter values. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable due to missing dependencies.

findings.title: Non-finite location indices are serialized into the route
findings.description: Math.max and Math.floor do not sanitize every JavaScript number: NaN becomes the literal query value "NaN", while positive Infinity becomes "Infinity". Although the reader later converts these values to index 0, the writer can still emit malformed, non-canonical route state, making its input invariant weaker than its number type suggests.
findings.recommendation: Validate locationIndex with Number.isFinite before flooring and clamping it, choosing a documented fallback such as 0 for non-finite values. Add unit cases for NaN, positive and negative Infinity, negative values, and fractional values.

grade.rationale: The utilities are concise, side-effect-free, and generally straightforward, but the fallback state policy is insertion-order-dependent and both traversals can fail on unusually deep input.

observations.summary: The implementation is readable and easy to test in isolation. Its main correctness risk is selecting an arbitrary kind as the node state when no code review exists; its main robustness risk is unbounded recursive traversal. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied.

findings.title: Fallback state depends on object property insertion order
findings.description: When a node has no code kind, its state is taken from the first value returned by Object.values(node.kinds). Although JavaScript enumeration order is deterministic for a given object, it reflects property construction order rather than an explicit review-kind priority or aggregation rule. Equivalent nodes assembled in different orders can therefore receive different states and UI presentation.
findings.recommendation: Define an explicit priority list or aggregation rule for non-code kinds and select the fallback state using that policy. Add tests covering multiple kind orders and nodes with no kinds.

findings.title: Deep trees can exhaust the JavaScript call stack
findings.description: Both functions recurse once per tree level without enforcing a depth limit or using an explicit work stack. A sufficiently deep tree can throw RangeError instead of returning a result, which is relevant if tree data can originate from unusually nested or malformed input.
findings.recommendation: Use iterative depth-first traversal with an explicit stack, or validate and cap input depth at the boundary. Include a deeply nested-tree test to verify the chosen behavior.

grade.rationale: The navigation update is concise and dependency-injected, but the embedded-message boundary has two material security and correctness weaknesses: it discloses the complete current URL and explicitly permits delivery regardless of the parent origin.

observations.summary: The function correctly updates preview parameters and is straightforward to test through its environment abstraction. However, its postMessage contract contradicts the stated data-minimization boundary by forwarding arbitrary existing URL content, and the wildcard target origin prevents authenticating the recipient. ESLint evidence was unavailable, and test coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Parent messages are sent without validating the recipient origin
findings.description: The message is always sent with `'*'` as its target origin, and the environment interface only permits that literal value. Any origin capable of embedding the preview can therefore receive its navigation messages, while a parent navigation race could also redirect a message to a different origin. This is especially risky because the payload contains a complete URL.
findings.recommendation: Determine an expected parent origin from trusted configuration or a validated embedding handshake, expose it through the environment contract, and pass that exact origin to `postMessage`. Reject or disable embedded reporting when no trusted origin is available.

findings.title: Navigation message exposes arbitrary existing URL data
findings.description: `url.href` includes the origin, fragment, user-information if present, and every pre-existing query parameter—not just `path`, `kind`, and `repo`. Consequently, the implementation cannot uphold the documented promise that the message carries no credentials or other sensitive content; tokens or unrelated state already present in `environment.href` would be forwarded to the parent.
findings.recommendation: Construct the reported URL from an allowlist of required navigation fields and an explicitly approved origin/path. Exclude unrelated query parameters, user-information, and the fragment unless each is part of the documented protocol.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet is functionally coherent, but its fixed-width detail layout can make the coverage table unusable on narrow screens, and several extremely small text sizes undermine readability. Minor maintainability and interaction-state issues also remain.

observations.summary: The modal and sticky coverage table are generally structured correctly. The main risks are the non-responsive 350px detail pane, typography as small as 6–8px, incomplete keyboard-focus styling, and repeated hard-coded semantic colors.

findings.title: Fixed detail column can collapse the table on narrow viewports
findings.description: When `.has-detail` is active, the grid always reserves 350px for the detail pane. On a phone-sized viewport, the remaining `minmax(0,1fr)` track can shrink to nearly zero, leaving the primary coverage table effectively unusable. The fixed 240px sticky boundary column further increases the minimum useful table width.
findings.recommendation: Add a responsive breakpoint that stacks the detail pane, turns it into an overlay, or replaces the fixed width with a bounded responsive track such as `minmax(260px, 35vw)`. Verify both table and detail interactions at narrow viewport widths.

findings.title: Interface labels use extremely small font sizes
findings.description: The stylesheet repeatedly uses 6–9px text; the cell flag is only 6px. At normal zoom this is difficult to read, particularly on high-density or small displays, and can impair users with reduced vision.
findings.recommendation: Raise informational labels to a practical minimum size, preferably using shared typography tokens and relative units. Preserve visual hierarchy through weight, color, and spacing rather than shrinking essential labels below readable sizes.

findings.title: Interactive coverage cells define hover feedback but no explicit focus feedback
findings.description: Coverage cells are pointer-interactive and receive a custom hover outline, but this stylesheet provides no corresponding `:focus-visible` state. Keyboard users therefore receive weaker or globally dependent feedback for the same interaction.
findings.recommendation: Add a clearly visible `.coverage-cell:focus-visible` style, ideally sharing the hover outline while retaining an accessible focus indicator. Apply the same interaction-state policy consistently to the other custom buttons.

findings.title: Semantic status colors are repeated as literals
findings.description: Finding and disagreement colors are embedded directly in multiple rules while other statuses use theme variables. This makes theme adaptation and coordinated contrast changes error-prone.
findings.recommendation: Define semantic variables such as `--status-finding`, `--status-finding-fg`, and `--status-disagreement`, then use them consistently in cells, flags, summaries, errors, and history borders.

grade.rationale: The template is generally well structured and presents loading, error, summary, detail, and empty-list states clearly. The main correctness risk is a potentially non-unique Angular tracking key for independent judgements; smaller weaknesses include a dead-end error state and render-time history transformations.

observations.summary: A solid Angular template with good semantic organization and accessible labels on interactive controls. It would benefit from stable judgement identities, an explicit retry path, and moving trajectory ordering out of the template.

findings.title: Judgement tracking key is not guaranteed to be unique
findings.description: The loop tracks each judgement only by reviewer agent and model. Multiple independent judgements can legitimately come from the same agent/model combination, producing duplicate keys. Angular may then report a duplicate-key error, recreate the affected collection, or associate rendered nodes with the wrong judgement when data changes.
findings.recommendation: Track judgements using a stable unique judgement or run identifier supplied by the model. If no such identifier exists and the list is immutable, use $index as an explicit fallback rather than claiming the reviewer fields form a unique identity.

findings.title: Coverage loading errors have no retry path
findings.description: When loading fails, the dialog displays the error but provides no recovery action. The only available response is closing the dialog, and it is unclear whether reopening it retries the operation.
findings.recommendation: Add a Retry button that invokes the coverage-loading operation, while retaining the alert semantics and close action.

findings.title: History is copied and reversed during template evaluation
findings.description: Calling slice().reverse() in the template allocates and transforms an array whenever the expression is reevaluated. It also leaves the required newest-first ordering implicit in view markup, making it harder to test independently.
findings.recommendation: Expose an already ordered history collection from the component, preferably through a computed signal or other memoized derivation, and iterate over that value in the template.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet is coherent and consistently uses shared design tokens, but the folder table has a responsive overflow defect that can make columns inaccessible.

observations.summary: The styling is generally well structured and maintainable. One confirmed correctness issue causes the folder table's fixed 1120px grid to be clipped without horizontal scrolling in narrower containers. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied, and the unavailable ESLint run provides no applicable CSS findings.

findings.title: Folder table columns can be clipped with no way to reach them
findings.description: The header and rows require at least 1120px of width, while the viewport declares a smaller 980px minimum and explicitly hides horizontal overflow. When the containing pane is narrower than 1120px, the rightmost columns extend beyond the visible area but no horizontal scrollbar is available, making their content and controls inaccessible.
findings.recommendation: Allow horizontal scrolling on the viewport with `overflow-x:auto`, and place both the column header and rows inside the same scrolling element so they remain horizontally aligned. Alternatively, replace the fixed minimum-width grid with a responsive column layout that fits the supported minimum pane width.

grade.rationale: The template is feature-rich and generally readable, but it contains several concrete interaction and accessibility defects, including unintended form submission, an inert close affordance, inaccessible form controls, incomplete table semantics, and no distinguishable file-load failure state. Test coverage is unknown, and ESLint evidence was unavailable.

observations.summary: The main rendering paths appear coherent, but several controls do not behave or announce themselves as their markup suggests. The most important fixes are to make every non-submit button explicit, expose load failures, label comment fields, and correct the interactive table and sorting semantics.

findings.title: Non-submit controls can submit an ancestor form
findings.description: The aspect tab and finding marker omit `type="button"`. HTML buttons default to submit buttons, so either control can unexpectedly submit a form that contains this component.
findings.recommendation: Add `type="button"` to both buttons and add a regression test that renders the editor inside a form and verifies that activating them does not submit it.

findings.title: Tab close affordance is inert and inaccessible
findings.description: The multiplication sign is styled and positioned like a tab close control but is only a span with no click or keyboard behavior and no accessible name. Users are given a familiar actionable affordance that cannot be activated.
findings.recommendation: If the tab is closable, replace the span with a `type="button"` control having an accessible name and a close handler. If it is decorative, remove it or hide it from assistive technology and avoid close-control styling.

findings.title: File-load failures are indistinguishable from having no file open
findings.description: The file view renders a loading message while loading and later falls through to `No file open`, but it contains no failure message or retry action. A rejected or failed request can therefore appear to the user as an intentional empty selection.
findings.recommendation: Expose the API error state in this template and render a descriptive alert with an appropriate retry action before falling back to the genuine no-selection state.

findings.title: Comment entry fields lack durable accessible names
findings.description: The reply input and new-comment textarea rely only on placeholder text. Placeholders disappear as users type and are not a reliable substitute for programmatically associated labels.
findings.recommendation: Give each field a visible `<label>` or an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` that identifies the thread or source line. Keep the placeholder only as optional input guidance.

findings.title: Table rows override button semantics
findings.description: Risk and folder entries are native buttons whose accessible role is replaced with `row`. This creates a hybrid control: assistive technology receives table-row semantics while the element is expected to behave as a button, so its action may not be announced consistently.
findings.recommendation: Use structural `role="row"` elements containing correctly scoped cells and place a real button or link inside the appropriate cell. Alternatively, use a semantic table or grid pattern with documented keyboard interaction.

findings.title: Sortable column headers do not expose their current sort direction
findings.description: The column headers visually append sort indicators, but none sets `aria-sort`. Screen-reader users cannot reliably determine which column controls the current order or whether it is ascending or descending.
findings.recommendation: Bind `aria-sort` on the active `columnheader` to `ascending` or `descending`, and set it to `none` or omit it for inactive columns. Test both table variants after changing sort direction.

findings.title: Review-aspect tabs lack complete tab interaction semantics
findings.description: The controls declare `tablist` and `tab` roles and expose selection, but they do not identify corresponding tab panels, manage a single tab stop, or show keyboard handling for moving between tabs. This does not implement the interaction users expect from an ARIA tab interface.
findings.recommendation: Implement the complete tabs pattern: associate each tab with its panel using IDs and `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby`, use roving `tabindex`, and support arrow-key navigation. If that behavior is not intended, present the controls as an ordinary labelled button group instead of tabs.

grade.rationale: The implementation is compact and readable, but its documented coordinate convention conflicts with its range conversion, potentially shifting most highlights. It also silently mishandles inconsistent token input and can report duplicate ranges from one finding as an overlap.

observations.summary: The pure, narrowly scoped API is easy to exercise, but the core offset semantics need correction or clarification. Input invariants and fingerprint uniqueness should be handled explicitly, and the repeated linear scans could become costly on unusually complex lines.

findings.title: Start columns are shifted despite the documented zero-based convention
findings.description: The function documents range columns as zero-based UTF-16 offsets, but subtracts one from every start column. For example, a documented range starting at column 2 begins at column 1, highlighting an extra code unit on the left. End columns are not adjusted, so the implementation is internally asymmetric as well.
findings.recommendation: Define whether endpoints are zero-based and end-exclusive or one-based and inclusive. If the documented zero-based, end-exclusive convention is intended, use `range.start.column` directly and clamp both endpoints. Otherwise, change the public documentation and types to state the actual convention explicitly.

findings.title: Duplicate ranges from one finding are classified as an overlap
findings.description: Overlap state is based on the number of covering intervals, while fingerprints are copied without deduplication. Duplicate input ranges—or overlapping ranges carrying the same fingerprint—therefore produce `state: 'overlap'` and repeated fingerprint values even though only one distinct finding is present.
findings.recommendation: Deduplicate covering fingerprints before deriving both `state` and `fingerprints`, and define overlap using the number of distinct fingerprints. Alternatively, document and validate that a fingerprint can never have overlapping ranges on the same line.

findings.title: Token/text inconsistencies silently produce invalid segmentation
findings.description: Token boundaries are accumulated independently of `text.length` and are not validated or clamped. If token text is longer than `text`, boundaries beyond the source text can yield empty or misleading segments; if it is shorter, the remaining source text inherits the last token's kind. The signature accepts `tokens` and `text` separately without documenting that their concatenated text must match exactly.
findings.recommendation: Establish and enforce the invariant that concatenating token text equals `text`. Prefer throwing or returning an explicit failure for inconsistent input; if recovery is required, clamp token cuts to the text and assign uncovered content a deliberate fallback kind.

findings.title: Every output segment rescans all intervals and token ends
findings.description: For each boundary pair, the implementation filters the complete interval list and performs a linear search through token ends. With B boundaries, R ranges, and T tokens, this is O(B×(R+T)), which can become quadratic on long or generated lines and may affect editor responsiveness.
findings.recommendation: Walk the sorted token ends with a moving index and use start/end events or an active-interval set for findings. This makes the segmentation pass approximately O((R+T) log R) or linear after sorting.

grade.rationale: The implementation is concise and generally handles cancellation and stale responses correctly, but an edge case defeats the cache bound, worker startup failures bypass the callback contract, and hard-coded browser dependencies make isolated testing unnecessarily difficult.

observations.summary: The main correctness concern is potentially unbounded cache growth when an empty path is cached. Error handling covers asynchronous worker errors but not synchronous construction or messaging failures. The structure is otherwise clear and easy to follow.

findings.title: An empty path disables cache eviction
findings.description: The eviction guard tests `oldest` by truthiness. If the oldest cache key is the empty string—which is allowed by the `string` API and can represent an untitled document—the condition remains false whenever eviction is attempted. That entry stays oldest and the cache can then grow beyond its intended four-entry bound indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Check whether the iterator is done or compare the key explicitly with `undefined`, rather than testing the string's truthiness. For example, retain the iterator result and delete its value when `!result.done`.

findings.title: Synchronous worker failures bypass the error callback
findings.description: The callback interface presents `error` as the failure channel, but both the Worker constructor and `postMessage` may throw synchronously, such as when worker creation is blocked or initialization data cannot be posted. In those cases `highlight` throws, may leave partially initialized state, and never invokes `callbacks.error`.
findings.recommendation: Wrap worker creation and initial `postMessage` in a try/catch. Clean up any worker that was created, clear the stored reference only if it still refers to that worker, and report a normalized message through `callbacks.error`.

findings.title: Worker creation and scheduling are hard-coded
findings.description: The service constructs the browser Worker directly and schedules cached delivery through the global timer API. Unit tests must patch global APIs and coordinate timer behavior, making worker failures, cancellation races, and chunk delivery harder to exercise deterministically.
findings.recommendation: Inject or encapsulate a worker factory and scheduling function, with production defaults using `Worker` and `setTimeout`. Tests can then provide deterministic fakes without modifying global state.

grade.rationale: The function is concise and handles nullish paths, case-insensitive extensions, and missing extensions well. However, lookup through a normal object's prototype can return values that are not SyntaxLanguage, violating the declared return contract for specially named extensions.

observations.summary: A small, readable implementation with one confirmed runtime correctness issue in its extension dictionary lookup. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable.

findings.title: Inherited object properties can be returned as syntax languages
findings.description: SYNTAX_LANGUAGE_BY_EXTENSION is a normal object, so indexing it accepts inherited keys in addition to configured extensions. For example, a path ending in `.constructor`, `.toString`, or `.__proto__` can produce a function or object rather than null. The Record type hides this runtime possibility, and nullish coalescing does not reject these non-null inherited values, violating the function's declared return type and potentially breaking downstream editor integration.
findings.recommendation: Use a prototype-free dictionary or an own-property check before returning the value, such as Object.hasOwn(SYNTAX_LANGUAGE_BY_EXTENSION, extension). Alternatively, use a Map. Add regression tests for prototype property names alongside normal, unknown, nullish, and extensionless paths.

grade.rationale: The module defines a concise, strongly discriminated message protocol and clear syntax-token types. No correctness or error-handling defects are evident in the supplied content; the only concern is inconsistent immutability in the token model.

observations.summary: Well-structured type definitions with clear discriminated unions and appropriately narrow literal types. Immutability is only partially expressed, allowing token data to be mutated despite TokenLine being readonly. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable due to a missing dependency.

findings.title: Token immutability is expressed inconsistently
findings.description: TokenLine prevents replacement of array elements, but each TokenSpan remains mutable, and chunk responses expose a mutable lines array. Consumers can therefore alter token text, kinds, or the chunk collection even though the readonly TokenLine alias suggests tokenization results are intended to be immutable. This weakens the contract and can allow accidental shared-state mutations in consumers and tests.
findings.recommendation: Make TokenSpan fields readonly and expose chunk lines as a readonly array, for example `readonly text`, `readonly kind`, and `lines: readonly TokenLine[]`. Apply the same convention consistently to other protocol fields if immutable message values are intended.

grade.rationale: The worker is concise, preserves multiline tokenizer state, chunks responses predictably, correlates them with request IDs, and reports tokenizer failures. Its main weakness is trusting an erased TypeScript message type at the worker boundary, allowing malformed messages to cause an uncaught exception before error handling begins.

observations.summary: The implementation is clear and largely correct. One low-severity robustness issue exists: incoming worker messages are dereferenced before runtime validation and outside the try/catch block. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable due to missing dependencies.

findings.title: Malformed worker messages can escape the error handler
findings.description: The MessageEvent generic provides compile-time typing only. At runtime, data may be null, undefined, or another unexpected value; reading data.kind then throws before entering the try block. This produces an uncaught worker error and no protocol-level error response. The risk is limited because worker messages normally originate from the owning application, but the worker boundary should still be defensive.
findings.recommendation: Validate that data is a non-null object before accessing kind, and validate the required fields for tokenize requests. Place request dispatch inside protected control flow; safely ignore messages that cannot be correlated, or return an error response when a valid requestId is available.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet is compact and generally coherent, but its focus styling can leave keyboard-focused tree rows without any visible focus indicator.

observations.summary: One medium-severity accessibility correctness issue was identified: the default focus outline is removed from every tree row, while the replacement is limited to rows that also have the separate `active` class. No test coverage conclusions were drawn because coverage data is unavailable.

findings.title: Keyboard focus can be invisible on non-active tree rows
findings.description: The rule removes the browser focus outline from every `.tree-row`, but the replacement `:focus-visible` outline applies only when the same row also has `.active`. If focus and active state ever diverge—for example during programmatic focus, initialization, or a state-update delay—the focused control has no visible focus indication.
findings.recommendation: Apply the replacement outline to `.tree-row:focus-visible` unconditionally. If active rows require distinct styling, add that styling separately without making basic focus visibility depend on the `active` class.

grade.rationale: The template is concise and uses appropriate Angular control flow, semantic buttons, ARIA tree roles, and stable tracking. Its main weaknesses are incomplete accessibility metadata for the virtualized tree and two small robustness/accessibility omissions on the refresh control.

observations.summary: The explorer template is generally clear and maintainable. Three issues were found: virtualized tree items do not expose their position and set size to assistive technology, the refresh button lacks a reliable accessible name, and it can unintentionally submit an enclosing form because its type is unspecified. Test coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Virtualized tree items omit set-size and position metadata
findings.description: Only visible rows are rendered, so assistive technology cannot infer each item's position or the number of siblings from the DOM. The tree items expose aria-level but not aria-posinset or aria-setsize, which can make navigation context incomplete or misleading as the rendered window changes.
findings.recommendation: Compute each node's one-based position and sibling count and bind them through aria-posinset and aria-setsize on every treeitem. Verify the resulting tree with keyboard navigation and a screen reader while scrolling and filtering.

findings.title: Refresh button has no reliable accessible name
findings.description: The control is labelled only by the ↻ glyph. Symbol pronunciation varies between screen readers and may not communicate that the button reloads the repository tree.
findings.recommendation: Add a descriptive accessible name such as aria-label="Refresh repository tree". A tooltip may also help sighted pointer users but should not replace the accessible name.

grade.rationale: The component is generally well structured and uses Angular signals effectively, but its virtualized focus handling can lose or unexpectedly reclaim keyboard focus, and filtered-tree navigation does not preserve hierarchical semantics. Browser-global telemetry also weakens isolation and robustness.

observations.summary: The implementation is clear and cohesive overall. The main risks are keyboard accessibility under virtualization, incorrect parent/child navigation while filtering, and tightly coupled diagnostic instrumentation. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied.

findings.title: Virtualization can remove the focused row without providing a replacement
findings.description: The rendered window is derived solely from scroll position, while focus restoration searches that window only for the existing activeId. If a user scrolls the focused row beyond the overscan region, Angular removes its DOM element and the restoration target is absent. The focus-out handler deliberately preserves treeHasFocus when relatedTarget is null, so focus can remain stranded outside the tree; later scrolling or rendering can also unexpectedly return focus to the old row.
findings.recommendation: Keep the active row rendered while it owns DOM focus, or re-anchor activeId to an appropriate visible row before recycling it. Distinguish DOM recycling from genuine null-relatedTarget focus departures, such as window deactivation or programmatic blur, so later renders do not steal focus.

findings.title: Arrow navigation treats unrelated filtered matches as parents or children
findings.description: Filtering flattens the entire expanded tree and then removes nonmatching rows. In that result set, the row after an expanded directory is not necessarily its child, yet ArrowRight selects it. ArrowLeft similarly chooses the nearest earlier row with a smaller depth, which may be an unrelated match rather than the node's ancestor. This makes keyboard navigation dependent on incidental result order and violates tree-navigation expectations.
findings.recommendation: Retain explicit parent relationships in filtered results and navigate only to a visible child or actual ancestor. Alternatively, present search results with list-style keyboard behavior and disable expansion-oriented Left/Right semantics while a query is active.

findings.title: Toggle behavior is coupled to unguarded browser-global telemetry
findings.description: Every expansion schedules a global requestAnimationFrame callback that directly invokes performance.measure and console.info. Tests and nonstandard rendering environments must provide all of these globals, and a failure in optional measurement code becomes an uncaught asynchronous error. Repeated measures are also retained unless another part of the application clears them.
findings.recommendation: Move telemetry behind an injectable service or small no-throw adapter with injectable clock and scheduler dependencies. Define a bounded policy for retained performance entries and clean up scheduled work when the component is destroyed.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet is generally coherent and uses shared design tokens effectively, but its hotspot table is not viable on narrow mobile viewports because minimum column widths exceed the available space while overflow is clipped.

observations.summary: The dashboard styling is mostly correct and consistently organized. One responsive-layout defect can hide hotspot data on small screens. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable due to missing dependencies.

findings.title: Hotspot columns are clipped on narrow mobile viewports
findings.description: At the 900px breakpoint, the five columns still require at least 464px, plus 32px of grid gaps and 20px of horizontal padding, for a total minimum width of 516px. On common mobile viewports the grid therefore overflows its container, while the container's `overflow:hidden` clips the excess. Users can lose access to the right-hand hotspot fields because no horizontal scrolling or alternative compact layout is provided.
findings.recommendation: At a smaller breakpoint, replace the row with a stacked or reduced-column layout. If retaining the table structure, wrap it in a container with `overflow-x:auto` instead of clipping it, and add visual regression tests at representative widths such as 320px and 375px.

grade.rationale: The template presents comprehensive loading, stale-data, empty, and failure states and uses clear repository-focused sections. Its main weaknesses are an ambiguous tracking key that can break list reconciliation and incomplete ARIA table semantics that obscure hotspot navigation for assistive technologies.

observations.summary: A solid dashboard template with two substantive correctness issues. The repository dependency loop can generate duplicate Angular tracking keys, while the hotspots table combines table and button semantics in a way that does not expose valid cells or actionable rows to assistive technology. The supplied build analyzer reported no findings; ESLint evidence was unavailable because its dependency was missing, so it provides no additional assurance. Test coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Concatenated dependency paths are not a unique tracking key
findings.description: The loop tracks each edge using `edge.sourcePath + edge.targetPath`. Distinct pairs can produce the same string—for example, `ab`→`c` and `a`→`bc`—causing duplicate Angular tracking keys and potentially incorrect DOM reuse or a runtime duplicate-key diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: Track a guaranteed unique edge identifier. If none exists, add one to the view model or track a collision-safe composite representation rather than undelimited concatenation.

findings.title: Hotspot table rows are neither valid table cells nor exposed actions
findings.description: The container declares `role="table"` and its children declare `role="row"`, but the descendant spans have no `columnheader` or `cell` roles. Assigning `role="row"` to each button also replaces its exposed button role, so assistive technology may neither understand the columns nor announce that a row is actionable. The empty paragraph is likewise placed directly inside the ARIA table without valid row/cell structure.
findings.recommendation: Prefer a native `<table>` with `<th>` and `<td>` elements and place a clearly labelled button or link inside a cell for navigation. If custom ARIA table markup is necessary, provide `rowgroup`, `columnheader`, and `cell` roles and expose row navigation through a separately identifiable keyboard-accessible control; render the empty state outside the table or in a valid row and cell.

grade.rationale: The component is concise, readable, and generally correct, with sensible fallbacks and reactive state. Its main weakness is using spread syntax with arrays of unbounded size when calculating maxima, which can fail for sufficiently large project data.

observations.summary: A clear, maintainable Angular component with one robustness issue in maximum-value calculations. ESLint evidence was unavailable, and test coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Maximum calculations spread unbounded arrays into function arguments
findings.description: Both maximum calculations pass every array element as a separate argument to Math.max. For sufficiently large hotspot or bucket collections, this can exceed the JavaScript engine's argument limit and throw a RangeError, preventing the dashboard from rendering. The fallback value of 1 only handles empty arrays; it does not mitigate argument-count limits.
findings.recommendation: Compute the maximum with an iterative reduction, such as `items.reduce((max, item) => Math.max(max, item.risk), 1)`, and use the equivalent approach for bucket counts. Add boundary tests with large collections.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet is coherent and uses shared design tokens consistently, but its fixed two-column layout can make the form unusable on narrow viewports, and the minified source formatting significantly reduces maintainability.

observations.summary: One responsive-layout correctness issue and one source-readability issue were identified. Error presentation is styled appropriately, but test coverage is unknown; the supplied ESLint analysis was unavailable because its dependency was missing.

findings.title: Fixed sidebar can collapse the form on narrow viewports
findings.description: The dialog width adapts to the viewport, but its first grid column always retains `--studio-modal-sidebar-width`. Once the available dialog width approaches or falls below that value, the `minmax(0,1fr)` form column can shrink to zero or become too narrow to use. The fieldset and footer controls have no compensating wrap or alternate mobile layout.
findings.recommendation: Add a narrow-viewport breakpoint that switches the body to a single-column layout or otherwise reduces/collapses the sidebar. Also allow option and action groups to wrap where necessary, and verify the dialog at representative mobile widths and enlarged text settings.

findings.title: Source stylesheet is stored in minified form
findings.description: Multiple selectors and all of their declarations are compressed onto long lines. This makes diffs harder to review, complicates precise diagnostics, and increases the chance of accidental edits affecting adjacent rules.
findings.recommendation: Format the source stylesheet with one declaration per line and conventional indentation. If minification is required for delivery, apply it only to generated build output through the existing build pipeline.

grade.rationale: The template is generally clear, well-structured, and uses appropriate form and dialog semantics. Its main weaknesses are incomplete whitespace validation, limited presentation of native validation failures, and a visually conveyed repository-selection state that is not exposed to assistive technology.

observations.summary: A solid dialog template with sensible labeling, constraints, event boundaries, and server-error announcement. Tightening validation and selection-state accessibility would improve correctness and usability.

findings.title: Whitespace-only required values can be submitted
findings.description: The save guard checks `form.displayName` and `form.rootPath` only for truthiness. HTML `required` validation also treats strings containing only whitespace as non-empty, so values such as `"   "` can enable the button and reach `saveRequested.emit()`. This can create invalid display names or repository paths unless every consumer independently normalizes them.
findings.recommendation: Normalize these values before validation and saving, or base the guard on trimmed values such as `!form.displayName.trim()` and `!form.rootPath.trim()`. Keep equivalent validation in the component or service as the authoritative boundary.

findings.title: Most field constraints have no persistent validation feedback
findings.description: The repository ID pattern and numeric minimum/maximum constraints rely entirely on browser-native constraint validation. The save button can appear enabled while these controls are invalid, and unlike the token-cap field they have no persistent, programmatically associated error message. Native validation bubbles vary by browser and are harder to test consistently.
findings.recommendation: Track the form or individual controls' validity, show actionable inline messages after interaction or submission, associate them with `aria-describedby`, and include invalid form state in the save-button or submit-handler guard.

findings.title: Selected repository state is exposed only through CSS
findings.description: The repository button receives an `active` class when selected, but no semantic state such as `aria-current` or `aria-pressed`. Screen-reader users therefore cannot determine which configured repository is currently being edited from the navigation controls.
findings.recommendation: Expose the same condition through an appropriate ARIA state, for example `[attr.aria-current]="repository.id === editingRepositoryId ? 'true' : null"`, while retaining the visual class.

grade.rationale: This is a concise, strongly typed presentational component API with no evident correctness defects in the supplied TypeScript. Inputs and outputs clearly separate state from user intents, and error and saving states are exposed explicitly.

observations.summary: No actionable issues were identified in the reviewed file. The class contains only declarative Angular bindings, uses specific domain types, and delegates behavior to its parent. Template behavior and automated coverage cannot be assessed from the supplied evidence.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet is organized around consistent design tokens and clear component-scoped selectors, but two layout defects can make validation feedback or preflight information unusable in constrained layouts.

observations.summary: The styling is generally coherent and maintainable. The principal risks are an absolutely positioned validation message that reserves no layout space and a three-column preflight grid with no narrow-container adaptation. Test coverage is unknown, and the supplied ESLint analyzer was unavailable because its dependency was missing.

findings.title: Validation messages reserve no layout space
findings.description: The field hint is absolutely positioned below `.cap-field`, so it does not contribute to the flex layout's height. When the action row wraps or another element follows closely, an invalid-field message can overlap the next row or adjacent content.
findings.recommendation: Keep the hint in normal flow, for example by making `.cap-field` a small grid or column flex container. If absolute positioning is required, explicitly reserve sufficient block-end space on the field or its containing row.

findings.title: Preflight facts lack a narrow-layout fallback
findings.description: The facts section always renders three columns. Because each track uses `minmax(0,1fr)`, a narrow host compresses the cards and clips or truncates their contents rather than rearranging them into readable rows.
findings.recommendation: Add a container or media query that changes the grid to two columns and then one column at appropriate widths, or use an auto-fitting layout with a meaningful minimum card width.

grade.rationale: The template is generally coherent and uses Angular control flow, semantic labels, and explicit button types well. Its main weaknesses are incomplete invalid-cap gating, run-control actions with no component-level pending/error path, repeated template computations, and one misleading accessible label. Test coverage is unknown, and ESLint evidence was unavailable.

observations.summary: The review UI is broadly correct and understandable, but invalid cap values can still reach the preflight action, run-control operations lack visible pending/error handling, repeated runFiles calls add unnecessary change-detection work, and the model-picker toggle has an inaccurate accessible name while open.

findings.title: Invalid cap values do not disable the preflight action
findings.description: The token-cap field exposes tokenCapError and the cost field declares a minimum, but the start button's disabled condition checks neither. Because prepare() is invoked by a standalone button rather than form submission, native number-input constraint validation will not prevent the click. The UI can therefore invoke preflight while displaying an invalid token cap or while the cost control is invalid, unless validation is redundantly enforced outside this template.
findings.recommendation: Expose a unified cap-valid signal and include it in the start button's disabled condition. Give the cost field explicit validation feedback and aria-invalid handling comparable to the token field, while retaining server-side validation as the final safeguard.

findings.title: Run-control actions have no local pending or failure state
findings.description: Pause, cancel, and resume call the API directly from the template. The controls remain enabled while an operation is outstanding, allowing duplicate requests, and this component has no evident place to surface a rejection or restore a consistent state. The direct dependency also makes interaction tests more tightly coupled to the API service.
findings.recommendation: Route each action through a component handler that tracks the pending action, disables conflicting controls, catches and exposes failures, and delegates to the API service. Add an accessible status or alert for failures.

findings.title: Model-picker toggle always announces an opening action
findings.description: The toggle's click behavior closes the picker when it is open, but its accessible name remains “Open model picker.” Screen-reader users therefore receive an inaccurate description of the action in the expanded state.
findings.recommendation: Bind the label to the picker state, for example “Close model picker” when expanded and “Open model picker” when collapsed.

findings.title: Each run-file category is recomputed repeatedly during rendering
findings.description: Each category calls runFiles once for the condition, again for the summary count, and again for iteration. Angular may reevaluate all of these expressions during change detection, multiplying filtering or allocation work and allowing inconsistent results if the method is not pure and stable.
findings.recommendation: Compute the categorized file collections once in component state or a computed signal, then bind the cached collection to the condition, count, and loop. This also gives tests a single transformation to exercise.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet appears functionally sound, but duplicated cascade rules and heavily compressed formatting make its intended behavior harder to verify and maintain. CSS-specific automated analysis was unavailable because ESLint dependencies were missing, and test coverage is unknown.

observations.summary: No critical correctness problems were identified. The main concerns are a conflicting duplicate grid declaration whose result depends on source order and dense formatting that obscures individual rules and increases review risk.

findings.title: Scan grid column count is defined twice with conflicting values
findings.description: The initial `.scan-grid` rule configures three columns, while a later rule changes the same property to four columns. The three-column declaration is therefore dead under the current source order, and moving or splitting these rules could silently change the layout.
findings.recommendation: Keep a single canonical `grid-template-columns` declaration with the intended four-column value, or place a context-specific override under a distinct selector or documented responsive condition.

findings.title: Multiple rules are compressed onto long source lines
findings.description: The stylesheet places complete adjacent rule sets on the same line and removes normal declaration spacing. This makes diffs, reviews, breakpoint debugging, and precise ownership of changes unnecessarily difficult.
findings.recommendation: Apply the project's CSS formatter so each selector block and declaration is consistently separated. Enforce that formatting in CI once the frontend linting dependencies are available.

grade.rationale: The template exposes a capable review workflow, but several inconsistent assumptions about optional data and finding identity can cause runtime failures or incorrect UI state. Accessibility and button semantics also need tightening.

observations.summary: The overall structure is functional but overly dense. The main risks are dereferencing an apparently optional grade, using inconsistent keys for findings and input traces, implicit submit buttons, and incomplete ARIA tab behavior. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable because dependencies were missing.

findings.title: Optional grade is dereferenced without a guard
findings.description: The header treats `activeMeta().grade` as optional, but the summary card dereferences `meta.grade.rationale`, `band`, and `score` whenever metadata exists. If metadata is available before its grade or legitimately lacks a grade, template evaluation will fail instead of rendering the existing fallback.
findings.recommendation: Guard the summary card with `@if (meta.grade; as grade)` and render a defined unavailable state otherwise, or make the data contract require a non-null grade and remove the contradictory optional access.

findings.title: Task status uses an identity that can be absent or collide
findings.description: Finding selection and tracking explicitly fall back from `fingerprint` to `id`, but task handover state is indexed only by `finding.id`. A fingerprint-only finding produces a shared `kind:undefined` key, so unrelated findings can display or inherit the same creation status.
findings.recommendation: Define one stable finding-key helper, such as `findingKey(finding)`, using the same fingerprint-or-id policy everywhere, and use it for selection, tracking, mutations, and handover status.

findings.title: Input trace lookup discards the input scope
findings.description: Inputs are tracked using the composite `scope:id` identity, indicating that the same ID can occur in multiple scopes, but finding counts are retrieved using only `input.id`. Duplicate IDs across scopes can therefore show the wrong trace count.
findings.recommendation: Key `inputTraces` by the same composite identity used by the loop, or expose a helper that accepts both `scope` and `id`.

findings.title: Action buttons rely on the implicit submit type
findings.description: Finding cards and the implementation-task action omit `type="button"`. If this component is ever rendered beneath a form element, activating either control will also submit that form.
findings.recommendation: Add `type="button"` to every button that is not intentionally a form submit control, and enforce this with template linting when dependencies are available.

findings.title: Thread filters declare tabs without implementing tab behavior
findings.description: The controls use `tablist` and `tab` roles but provide no associated `tabpanel`, `aria-controls`, stable tab IDs, roving tabindex, or arrow-key navigation. This exposes an incomplete tabs interaction model to assistive technology.
findings.recommendation: Either implement the complete ARIA tabs pattern, including keyboard navigation and an associated tab panel, or remove the tab roles and present the controls as an ordinary labeled button group with pressed-state semantics.

grade.rationale: The component is generally readable and uses Angular signals coherently, but several asynchronous workflows can commit stale state, and the scope-rule flow can save inputs different from those the user previewed. Error recovery also has a path that rejects unexpectedly.

observations.summary: The main risks are stale scope previews, out-of-order run-detail responses, an undo timer race, and incomplete handling when conflict recovery itself fails. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable because dependencies were missing.

findings.title: A scope rule can differ from the rule that was previewed
findings.description: saveScopeRule only checks that some preview exists, then constructs the saved request from the current action, pattern, and reason. Those inputs can change after previewing without invalidating scopePreview, so the user can save a different rule without reviewing its matched paths or satisfying the wider-pattern confirmation associated with it. Concurrent preview requests can similarly leave an older response as the current preview.
findings.recommendation: Bind each preview to an immutable snapshot or revision of action, pattern, and reason. Invalidate the preview whenever an input changes, discard responses whose revision is no longer current, and only save the exact snapshot represented by the accepted preview.

findings.title: Older run requests can overwrite the currently selected run
findings.description: openRun unconditionally stores report and trend results after awaiting them. If the user opens another run, opens a nonterminal run, or closes the detail view before an earlier request completes, that earlier request can repopulate the state and can also clear the loading flag while a newer request remains active.
findings.recommendation: Associate each load with a request token or the selected run ID and verify it before every state update, including loading and error updates. Alternatively, cancel superseded requests through the API layer.

findings.title: An old timeout can clear a newer undo operation
findings.description: The timeout identifies its mutation only by fingerprint. If the same finding is mutated again before the first eight-second timeout fires, the old callback sees the same fingerprint and clears the newer LastFindingMutation, shortening or eliminating its undo window.
findings.recommendation: Assign every mutation a unique generation or token and have the timeout compare that identity, or retain and cancel the previous timeout before scheduling a new one.

findings.title: Failure while recovering from a conflict escapes the method
findings.description: The 409 handler awaits loadFile from inside the original catch block without its own error handling. If the reload fails, setFindingState rejects, the status may remain "Saving…", and the user does not receive the API's error message.
findings.recommendation: Wrap conflict recovery in a nested try/catch or move it into a helper that always produces a final status. Report both that the mutation conflicted and that refreshing the current state failed.

grade.rationale: The stylesheet is coherent and uses sensible component structure, but the modal's default content-box height arithmetic can clip part of the scrollable region, and several labels use text sizes that are difficult to read. The highly compressed formatting also reduces maintainability.

observations.summary: The primary correctness issue is that the dialog, header, and content heights include padding differently under the default content-box model, allowing the parent’s hidden overflow to obscure the bottom of long content. Very small fixed font sizes also impair readability. No coverage data was available, so test coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Content-box height calculations can clip the scrollable region
findings.description: The header has an explicit 66px height plus 24px of vertical padding, while the content has a viewport-derived max-height plus 32px of vertical padding. Under the default content-box model, their outer heights can exceed the dialog's max-height. Because the dialog uses overflow:hidden, the bottom of the content's own scrolling box can be clipped and become unreachable when the history is long. This only works safely if an undocumented global border-box rule happens to apply.
findings.recommendation: Make the dialog a column flex container with box-sizing:border-box, give the header a non-growing size, and use flex:1; min-height:0; overflow:auto on the content. Alternatively, explicitly include padding and borders in every height calculation, though the flex approach is less fragile.

findings.title: Multiple interface labels are rendered at only 8–9px
findings.description: Metadata and definition labels repeatedly use 8px or 9px text. At normal browser zoom these sizes are difficult to read, especially on high-density or small displays, and uppercase transformation further reduces legibility.
findings.recommendation: Use the project's accessible typography tokens where available and raise secondary labels to a readable baseline, generally at least 11–12px. Validate the dialog at browser zoom levels up to 200%.

grade.rationale: The template is clear, semantically structured, and provides useful empty states and accessible labels. Its main weaknesses are unstable disclosure state based on array positions and an ARIA reference whose target is removed when collapsed.

observations.summary: The usage-history dialog is generally well organized and readable. Two issues should be addressed: recent-entry expansion is keyed by a mutable array index, and collapsed entries retain aria-controls references to elements that do not exist. Test coverage is unknown, and the unavailable ESLint result does not establish a defect.

findings.title: Expanded entry state is tied to the array index
findings.description: The disclosure state compares expandedEntry() with the current loop index. If recent entries are inserted, removed, or reordered while the dialog is open, the same numeric index can refer to a different entry, causing unrelated details to appear expanded. This also conflicts with the loop's attempt to preserve entry identity through its track expression.
findings.recommendation: Store and compare a stable entry identifier, such as a guaranteed-unique ledger entry ID, and derive aria-controls and panel IDs from that identifier instead of the array index.

findings.title: Collapsed disclosures reference absent control targets
findings.description: aria-controls is always emitted on each summary button, but its referenced details element is only created while the entry is expanded. In the collapsed state, the ID reference therefore has no target in the accessibility tree or DOM.
findings.recommendation: Keep each details container in the DOM and hide it when collapsed, or only emit aria-controls while its target exists. Continue keeping aria-expanded synchronized with the visible state.

grade.rationale: The component is concise and generally correct, but date formatting can throw on malformed API values and the hand-built focus trap can select elements that are not actually tabbable. The remaining logic is readable and reasonably testable, although browser globals and formatting helpers warrant focused unit tests.

observations.summary: Two robustness issues were identified: invalid date strings can break template rendering, and the focus-trap selector does not reliably model the browser's tab order. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied.

findings.title: Invalid date values can throw during rendering
findings.description: Both date helpers construct a Date and immediately pass it to Intl.DateTimeFormat.format(). If an API value is empty, malformed, or otherwise invalid, format() throws a RangeError. When these methods are invoked from the template, one bad usage record can interrupt change detection and prevent the history view from rendering.
findings.recommendation: Parse and validate the date before formatting, for example by checking Number.isNaN(date.getTime()), and return a consistent fallback such as "Unavailable" for invalid values. Add tests covering malformed, empty, and valid timestamp/day inputs.

findings.title: Focus trap can target elements outside the sequential tab order
findings.description: The selector includes hidden elements and any tabindex except the literal value -1, including negative values such as -2. Calling focus() on an invisible candidate may do nothing, while focusing another negative-tabindex candidate introduces it into keyboard traversal unexpectedly. Either case can make the modal's Tab boundary behavior inconsistent or allow focus to escape.
findings.recommendation: Use a proven dialog/focus-trap primitive, or filter candidates for visibility, inert/disabled state, and a non-negative effective tabIndex before choosing the first and last elements. Add keyboard tests for hidden controls, negative tabindex values, forward Tab, and Shift+Tab.
